title: Redundant Namespace Prefixing
pattern: Prefixing struct field names, enum variant names, or module-level function names with the name of the containing type or module.
why_bad: It introduces redundant name repetition and ceremony. Since field names are always accessed via their containing struct instances (e.g., `user.user_id`), prefixing them with the type name results in stuttering (`user.user_id`), adding visual noise and extra typing for zero informational gain.
detection: A field inside a struct or an enum variant whose identifier starts with the lowercase name of its containing struct or enum type.
counterexample: Public functions or traits in a nested submodule that explicitly include the submodule's name to resolve disambiguation in foreign modules.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 11 ("Power of Cognitive Names"), pp. 273-275.
